target: Primer Tooltip label versus description, directional placement and delay settings
observed_behavior: Primer's Tooltip product props distinguish type='label' (text identifies the trigger) from the default type='description' (text supplies supplementary context). The documented direction options are compass-like placements around the trigger, with default south alignment; product prose says placement can adjust to available viewport space, and an example sets east position. The props also offer optional keybindingHint and show-delay settings: short 50 ms (default), medium 400 ms, and long 1200 ms. These are component API statements and display intentions, not measured guarantees of fit or accessible output.
context: W07 Stage B5 K3; authorized Primer product page section: Tooltip React examples — label/positioned; Props — Tooltip. Explanatory product API/design documentation within Primer only.
limitations: The label versus description distinction is a Primer component option, not proof of a particular screen-reader announcement or accessible-name computation in a browser.
Viewport-aware placement is publisher-described behavior, not an independently tested guarantee at all zoom levels or orientations.
Delay numbers are documented option values, not timed measurements performed in this work.
Custom direction and keybinding hints are optional and task-specific; no universal label, delay or placement should be synthesized in K3.
